title: Welcome to Zillow Preferred

slides.title: Welcome to Zillow Preferred
slides.lead: Zillow Preferred · Day 1
slides.body:
Find the contact.
Update the record.
Set the follow-up.

Today’s practiceUpdate a contact record another agent can understand.Work with a partner. Give specific feedback. Try again.
slides.notes: Invite a recent example from one person, then begin. Keep the opening to two minutes.
slides.cue: Ask: What would you like to get better at today?

slides.title: What should the next agent know?
slides.lead: A useful record explains what happened and what comes next.
slides.body:
“I spoke with Avery. They want to compare two homes on Thursday.”

What is still missing?
slides.notes: Ask everyone to choose before revealing. Hear two explanations. Keep this distinction for the later repair exercise.
slides.cue: What would you need before calling Avery?

slides.title: What we will practice over four days
slides.lead: Today starts with the record you use every day.
slides.body:
Day 1 · Follow Up Boss

Find the lead, choose the true stage, write a note, and set a dated task.

Day 2 · The first call

Introduce yourself, invite the buyer early, listen, and summarize.

Day 3 · The showing

Learn what the buyer liked, what is missing, and their timing.

Day 4 · Zillow Home Loans

Explain the option, ask permission, and follow up on the introduction.
slides.notes: Keep this overview brief. Ask which task an agent already does comfortably. Do not reteach later modules here.
slides.cue: Which part of your current process needs the most practice?

slides.title: How a Zillow lead reaches you
slides.lead: Start with the Follow Up Boss contact record.
slides.body:
Live connection

You are connected with a buyer. Find the matching record before updating it.

Tour request

Read the property and requested time. A request alone is not a confirmed appointment.

Touring alert

Read what happened and what response is needed. Check the existing history.
slides.notes: Use your actual team routing process for the demonstration. Do not assume every notification means the same thing.
slides.cue: What would tell you that you have the correct record?

slides.title: Start in People
slides.lead: Use the actual contact name, source, and activity to find the record.
slides.notes: Demonstrate People, smart lists, and filtering in your training account. Open the image at full size if labels are hard to see. Ask an agent to point to the source and most recent activity.
slides.cue: Where would you look for a new Zillow contact?

slides.title: Find Avery in the training account
slides.lead: Confirm the source before opening or editing a record.
slides.body:
Find the name

Search for Avery in the training pond.

Check the source

Look for Zillow. If needed, use Filters → Add filter → Lead Source.

Open and confirm

Read the contact details and activity. Make sure this is the right Avery.
slides.notes: Have an agent narrate where they would click. Use the training account, never a live contact as a practice record.
slides.cue: Explain your first three clicks.

slides.title: Read before you change anything
slides.lead: Look for facts that affect the next conversation.
slides.body:
Who is this?

Confirm name and contact details.

Where did this start?

Check source and property context.

What already happened?

Read the recent calls, notes, and appointment history.

What is due next?

Check the assigned person and dated task.
slides.notes: Show a contact and allow 20 seconds of silent reading. Ask what is known and what still needs a question.
slides.cue: What would be risky to assume?

slides.title: Check the Details panel
slides.lead: The stage should match what actually happened.
slides.notes: Point out Stage, Assigned, Source, and Timeframe without narrating every control. Timing should come from the buyer, not a guess.
slides.cue: Which detail would you verify before saving?

slides.title: Separate facts from assumptions
slides.lead: Use background information to ask a question.
slides.body:
A fact

“Avery asked to see two homes on Thursday.”

An assumption

“Avery must be ready to buy this week.”

A useful question

“What is prompting your move, and is there a date you are working toward?”
slides.notes: Ask for two examples. Do not infer finances, family circumstances, or housing preferences from a profile. Keep the record factual.
slides.cue: Which words in a note tell you someone is guessing?

slides.title: Choose the stage that matches the event
slides.lead: Save the change and reopen the record to check it.
slides.body:
Before an appointment

Lead → Attempted contact → Spoke with customer → Appointment set. Use only what happened.

After meeting

Met with customer after the first appointment. Showing homes after the second appointment.

Offer and closing

Submitting offers when submitting. Under contract after acceptance, with the deal recorded. Closed after closing.
slides.notes: Show the full stage menu in the exercise. Explain this is the team’s stage mapping. A request for Thursday is not an appointment until a time is agreed. Demonstrate the green save check and reopening.
slides.cue: Which stage would you use after a voicemail?

slides.title: Choose Avery’s stage
slides.lead: Avery answered and asked about Thursday, but no time is booked.
slides.body: Which stage matches?
slides.notes: Ask agents to explain the evidence for their answer. Do not accept a label without the event behind it.
slides.cue: What new fact would justify Appointment set?

slides.title: Check the other examples
slides.lead: Explain the event before naming the stage.
slides.body:
New contact, no attempt yet

Lead.

Called and left a voicemail

Attempted contact.

Spoke about two homes

Spoke with customer.

Agreed Thursday at 3 p.m.

Appointment set. Save the change and check it.
slides.notes: Hide the answers first by asking verbally. Call on different agents. Next, each learner will make the appointment update in the existing record exercise.
slides.cue: Close your notes: what separates the last two?

slides.title: Practice: save the appointment stage
slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction.
slides.cue: Make the update, save it, then check your work.

slides.title: Write what the next agent needs
slides.lead: Record what happened, what the buyer said, and the agreed next step.
slides.body:
“Spoke with Avery. Looking for three bedrooms in Tacoma in 60–90 days. I’ll send two homes on Thursday, then call to compare them.”

Keep the facts

Use the buyer’s words where they clarify a need.

Make the next step specific

Name the action and agreed date.

Leave out guesses

A friendly conversation is not proof of readiness or budget.
slides.notes: Ask what the example tells the next caller. Then complete the note exercise. Coach one missing fact rather than rewriting the entire note for the agent.
slides.cue: Could someone follow up using only this note?

slides.title: Practice: write the conversation note
slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction.
slides.cue: Make the update, save it, then check your work.

slides.title: Give the follow-up a date and time
slides.lead: Write an action you will recognize when it comes due.
slides.body:
Too vague

“Follow up.”

Useful

“Call Avery to compare 406 and 422 Juniper — Thursday, 3 p.m.”

Before you leave

Confirm one clear next task with the correct date and time.
slides.notes: Explain the difference between a note and a task. The note records history; the task schedules the next action. Complete the missed-call exercise next.
slides.cue: What makes a task usable tomorrow?

slides.title: Practice: set the missed-call task
slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction.
slides.cue: Make the update, save it, then check your work.

slides.title: Repair Avery’s record
slides.lead: Only a request to compare homes is confirmed. The record says Appointment set.
slides.body:
What happened

Avery asked to compare 406 and 422 Juniper on Thursday. No appointment was booked.

What is wrong

The stage claims an appointment. The note is vague. There is no dated task.
slides.notes: Have agents diagnose first, then complete the repair exercise. Ask for evidence behind each change. The existing exercise checks the diagnosis before allowing edits.
slides.cue: What would you fix first, and why?

slides.title: Practice: repair Avery’s record
slides.lead: Use the training contact. Check your work to continue.
slides.notes: Let the agent find the control before offering a hint. Ask them to explain any correction.
slides.cue: Make the update, save it, then check your work.

slides.title: Check the record before moving on
slides.lead: Reopen what you saved.
slides.body:
Stage

Does it match the event, and did the change save?

Note

Does it explain what happened without guessing?

Task

Is the next action scheduled for a real date and time?

Handoff

Could another agent act on this record without asking you to explain it?
slides.notes: Ask agents to check their own work. Introduce the deal exercise: once an offer is accepted, update the stage and record the deal details.
slides.cue: Which check would catch an unsaved stage?

slides.title: Practice adding a deal
slides.lead: Use the buyer’s name, price, and expected close date.
slides.notes: Demonstrate the deal form, then let the learner enter it. Use fictional details.
slides.cue: What would you check before creating this deal?

slides.title: Practice: record the accepted offer
slides.lead: Update the stage and add the deal from the scenario.
slides.notes: Check the accepted-offer exercise. A passed check should explain the evidence, not just display a result.
slides.cue: What changed after the offer was accepted?

slides.title: Where will you start tomorrow?
slides.lead: Use your tasks and new leads to plan the next calls.
slides.body:
Due tasks

Review what you agreed to do and when.

New leads

Find the correct contact and read the history.

After each conversation

Update the stage, note, and dated next task.
slides.notes: Give 30 seconds without notes. Then ask partners to compare. Revisit only the missing item, not the entire lesson.
slides.cue: Explain your first five minutes in Follow Up Boss.

slides.title: Before your next client conversation
slides.lead: Write down when you will practice again.
slides.body:
Today

Complete the five record exercises and review any correction.

Before Day 2

Find a training contact, read the history, and explain what is due next.

With your coach

Review one real record together after your next client conversation.
slides.notes: Ask each agent to name one behavior they will practice. Within 24 hours, ask them to explain it without notes. In three days, use a new scenario. In seven days, review an actual example. These are suggested coaching intervals; no reminders are sent.
slides.cue: Tell your partner what you will practice and when.
